**Focus: Insurance Law-Civil Procedure**

Kutrubis was the owner of a life insurance policy that initially designated the trustee of his trust as the beneficiary. As his health deteriorated, Lambros sought to change the beneficiary designation to his ex-wife, Betty Stokes, and his adopted son, John Kutrubis. He dictated and signed a written request for the change in the presence of two witnesses and a notary. At Lambros’s direction, a friend mailed the request to the insurer, Banner Life Insurance Company. After Lambros died, however, Banner had no record of receiving the request before his death. Betty and John claimed entitlement to the policy proceeds based on Lambros’s written request, while Eugenia Kamberos, Lambros’s sister and the trustee of his trust, also asserted a claim. Banner filed an interpleader action seeking a determination of the proper recipient of the insurance proceeds.

The Northern District of Illinois, Eastern Division, considered the competing claims. As his health deteriorated, Lambros sought to change the beneficiary designation to his ex-wife, Betty Stokes, and his adopted son, John Kutrubis. He dictated and signed a written request for the change in the presence of two witnesses and a notary. At Lambros’s direction, a friend mailed the request to the insurer, Banner Life Insurance Company. After Lambros died, however, Banner had no record of receiving the request before his death. Betty and John claimed entitlement to the policy proceeds based on Lambros’s written request, while Eugenia Kamberos, Lambros’s sister and the trustee of his trust, also asserted a claim.
